verbalization: Doxorubicin is associated with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) through a series of indications that link it to AML subtypes with T(9;11)(p22;q23) chromosomal translocations, which are commonly found in AML with Cebpa somatic mutations. This relationship is supported by multiple pathways, where Doxorubicin is indicated for AML with T(9;11)(p22;q23), and this condition is further linked to AML with Cebpa mutations through different drugs, such as Gemtuzumab Ozogamicin and Idarubicin. The evidence suggests that Doxorubicin may be used in the treatment of AML with Cebpa mutations, though the exact mechanism of action and therapeutic relevance remain to be fully elucidated. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of support for this relationship, but further clinical studies are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety in this patient population.
